info.desc: Dookie is the third studio album and the major label debut by American Alternative rock band Green Day. The album was the band's first collaboration with producer Rob Cavallo. Released on February 1st, 1994 through Reprise Records, Dookie became a worldwide commercial success, reaching number two on the U.S. Billboard 200 and charting in seven countries. The album helped to propel Green Day into mainstream popularity, amid claims from the punk rock community that the band had "sold out". Dookie produced five singles for the band: "Longview", the re-recorded "Welcome to Paradise", "Basket Case", the radio-only single "She" and "When .

podcast.body: Released on February 1, 1994, this album achieved immense success, staying on the charts for two years and selling more than 10 million copies. It served as the major entry point for most of the world to Green Day and was instrumental in paving the way for numerous pop-punk bands like Sum 41, Blink-182, Good Charlotte, and Simple Plan. Some observers referred to it as "the punk rock version of The Joshua Tree," while others derisively called it "Flukey." "On February 1, 1994, Green Day released a record called Duckey. They knew it was pretty good, but no one expected it to stay on the charts for two years and sell more than 10 million copies."

podcast.body: Released on February 1, 1994, through Reprise Records, a label originally created by Frank Sinatra. The album initially sold slowly, moving only 9,000 copies in its first week. However, its sales trajectory changed significantly after Kurt Cobain's death two months later, as the music scene shifted away from the bleakness of grunge. By the summer of 1994, Dookie peaked at number 2 on the Billboard charts and achieved number one status in Canada, Australia, and New Zealand, also reaching the top 10 in several other countries. It has since sold at least 20 million units. "By the summer of 1994, that Duckey album peaked at number 2 in the Billboard charts, and was the number one hit in Canada, Australia, and New Zealand."

podcast.body: This album is considered one of the best albums of the 90s and an icon of modern music. It was Grimbey's second or third album, depending on how one counts their previous underground releases and an earlier initial disk. It was co-produced by the band and, for the first time, by an external professional, Rob Cavallo from Reprise Records. Dookie became Grimbey's best-selling album, with over 20 million copies sold, and is their only album to achieve diamond certification. It also received the Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album. podcast.body: Warner Bros. expected so little from Green Day's major label debut that only 9,000 copies were sent to stores on release day. The label's ceiling for success was 200,000 copies. The first single "Longview" had its MTV video debut on February 22; by the end of March the album was rising on the charts. When Kurt Cobain died on April 8, 1994, the shock created a vacuum in the alt-rock world — and *Dookie*'s punk energy helped fill it. By year's end it had gone multi-platinum; it was later certified Diamond (10 million in the US alone); worldwide sales reached approximately 20 million. It set off the mid-1990s punk pop revival, influencing the Offspring, Rancid, Sum 41, Blink-182, Fall Out Boy, and others. *Dookie* was also the first album Lady Gaga ever bought with her own money. Time Magazine ranked its influence alongside *Nevermind*. "This record acted as something of a bomb to the hearts broken by the end of Nirvana."

podcast.title: Breakthrough Album
podcast.body: Released on February 1, 1994, *Dookie* initially received good reviews but truly exploded after Kurt Cobain's death two months later, filling a void in the music scene. Its sound combined the rebelliousness of grunge with a fun, snotty attitude, distinguishing it from the doom and gloom of its predecessor genre. The album stayed on the charts for two years, selling over 20 million copies worldwide, won a Grammy for Best Alternative Album, and became a defining record for a generation, often cited as a life-changing album and a "gateway drug" to punk rock. "On February 1, 1994, a record called Duckey appeared in stores. And it got some good reviews. Then two months later, Kurt dies. A void. A vacuum opened up. And Green Day got sucked into it."
